disposition_reason: Peer-reviewed Food Control paper (PDF on disk is misnamed 'Villa 2014' but the content is Ferreira de Oliveira et al. 2021, DOI 10.1016/j.foodcont.2020.107455). Reports Cd and Pb in 90 fermented/dried bean batches by growing region (Table 2) and Cd/Pb in shell, liquor, cocoa powder and cocoa butter from one pilot-processed Bahia batch with a Cd mass balance (§3.3), plus a worst-case exposure scenario (Table 4).

study.design: farm-batch survey plus single pilot-scale processing study
study.material_scope: fermented and dried cocoa beans (homogenized with shells); pilot-derived shell, liquor, cocoa powder, cocoa butter
study.growing_origin_vs_market: Beans grown in Brazil (Bahia n=33, Pará n=29, Espírito Santo n=4, Rondônia n=8), Côte d'Ivoire (n=12) and Ecuador (n=4); 'acquired from different locations'; analysed in Campinas, Brazil. No retail market component.
study.sampling_unit: batch of beans from the same farm (one sample per farm batch)
study.method: Dry ashing (450 °C, 15 h, HCl) then ICP OES (Agilent 5100 VDV, axial; Cd 214.439 nm, Pb 220.353 nm), triplicate; microwave HNO3/H2O2 digestion evaluated and found equivalent
study.lod_loq: Cd LOD 0.0005 mg/kg, LOQ 0.0015 mg/kg; Pb LOD 0.007 mg/kg, LOQ 0.022 mg/kg (Table 1B; LOD=3s, LOQ=10s of 10 blanks)
study.basis: as analysed (beans with shell); no dry-weight or moisture basis stated
study.qa: CRM INCT-TL-1 Tea Leaves recoveries: microwave Cd 107 ± 5%, Pb 86 ± 6%; dry ashing Cd 103 ± 14%, Pb 86 ± 9%. NIST 1547 Peach Leaves (dry ashing): Cd 104 ± 9%, Pb 90 ± 5%. CV (n=6 bean replicates) Cd 3%, Pb 6%.

controls.control: Pilot-scale processing partition of Cd (roast, crush, winnow, grind to liquor, press)
controls.design: processing study (single pilot batch, no replication)
controls.outcome: Cd shell 0.124 ± 0.004; liquor 0.060 ± 0.006 (-47% vs beans); cocoa powder 0.111 ± 0.010 (-2% vs beans; ~1.85x liquor); cocoa butter <0.0015 mg/kg. Pb: shell 0.142 ± 0.006, liquor/powder/butter <0.022 mg/kg (bean Pb for this batch not reported).
controls.scale: pilot (2 kg beans; 500 g liquor pressed)

controls.control: Cd mass balance across grinding and pressing
controls.comparator: total Cd mass entering each step
controls.outcome: Grinding: 59% of Cd retained in mill residue, 35% to liquor, 6% to shell. Pressing: 100% of liquor Cd to cocoa powder; butter and press residue 0%. Cd concentrates in non-lipid (cocoa solids) fraction; butter essentially Cd-free.

controls.control: Blending beans from different origins to lower Cd/Pb in finished products
controls.design: survey (author recommendation inferred from regional differences; not tested)
controls.outcome: Not measured. Rationale: Ecuador beans Cd mean 1.153 mg/kg vs 0.038–0.142 mg/kg for Brazilian/Côte d'Ivoire groups; Pb highest in Pará (0.985) and Bahia (0.727) vs Ecuador 0.019 mg/kg, so the low-Cd and low-Pb origins differ.

controls.control: Origin selection (growing region) as a sourcing lever

contradictions_with_stored_summary: Stored summary lists 'nibs' among pilot-processed fractions with measured outputs; the primary reports no nib concentration (only beans, shell, liquor, powder, butter).
Stored summary states values are 'on a dry-bean basis'; the primary does not state a dry-weight basis (beans analysed as homogenized with shell).
Stored summary says butter and press residue were 'Cd-free at the LOD'; the primary reports butter as <0.0015 mg/kg, which is the LOQ (LOD 0.0005).
Stored summary describes the mill residue as 'a viscous residue inside the Melanger mill'; primary says only 'residue in the mill'.
Stored summary 'All n=90' Cd lower bound <0.0015 matches the abstract, but Table 2 and §3.2 print <0.015 (tenfold inconsistency not flagged in summary).
Raw file name says Villa 2014; content is Oliveira 2021 (summary already notes this).
unresolved: Supplementary Fig. S1 (per-region distributions) not available on disk; per-sample values not printed in the article.
Pb in the starting beans of the processing batch not reported, so Pb partitioning cannot be computed.
Treatment of <LOQ results in means (BA, CI, RO, EQ) not described; EQ Pb mean 0.019 is below LOQ.
Whether the method-comparison Bahia bean sample (Cd 0.056, Pb 2.43 mg/kg) is one of the 33 Bahia samples is not stated.

The processing study reports Cd liquor (0.060) about half of beans (0.113) with 59% of Cd 'retained in mill residue'; nib concentration was not measured, so the shell/nib split and residue loss cannot be independently checked.
